body_mass_kg.note: BVAD reference crewmember, mean male astronaut circa 2015. Real crews vary.

potable_water_kg_per_cm_d.note: 0.5 food prep + 2.00 drink + 0.717 exercise-related, BVAD Table 3-31.

food_logistics_kg_per_cm_d.note: ISS planning mass including packaging, as discussed in BVAD from Ewert et al. 2019. Not the dry edible mass.

water_recovery_iss_before_bpa.note: NASA: 93–94% before the brine processor. Midpoint 0.935 used when a single number is required.

electrolysis_kwh_per_kg_o2.note: Practical figure above the ~4 kWh/kg thermodynamic order. Not a named flight unit's measured specific energy.

farm_dry_edible_kg_per_m2_d.note: Order-of-magnitude controlled-environment rate for calorie crops, not a record lettuce yield. Lettuce fresh mass is a poor calorie proxy.

farm_light_kwe_per_m2.note: Electric lighting load. Sunlight greenhouses on the Moon/Mars still need power for the long night or dust season and for thermal control.

habitat_base_kwe.note: Small habitat hotel load, far below the ISS (~75–90 kW for a much larger pressurized volume).

o2_from_plants_kg_per_kg_dry_food.note: Rough stoichiometric company of edible dry biomass. Inedible biomass and RQ make this an estimate.

cruise_mgy_per_day.note: Inside MSL, RTG subtracted. Not free-space and not a naked EVA.

mars_surface_mSv_per_day.note: Rover-deck environment near solar maximum. Habitat regolith is extra shielding on top of this reference, not a replacement for it.

shortest_roundtrip_Sv.note: Published comparison for a short round trip with similar shielding. It does NOT include a 500-day surface stay.

lunar_surface_mSv_per_day.note: Half-sky planetary shielding on an airless body, solar-max order of magnitude. Not a CRaTER data product. MSL cruise is the measured anchor; this lunar number is an estimate.

shield_scale_g_cm2.note: Game transmission = 1 / (1 + extra_g_cm2 / 50). This is NOT HZETRN. GCR does not attenuate as a pure exponential; secondaries matter. Zero extra shielding reproduces the published reference rates.

storm_shelter_extra_g_cm2.note: Modest polyethylene/water shelter used as a sleep station on a transfer vehicle. It is additional to MSL-like vehicle shielding already inside the cruise rate.

buried_habitat_extra_g_cm2.note: Roughly under a meter of regolith depending on density. Permanent residence wants still more; see the 20 mSv/year design target.

career_planning_cap_mSv.note: Conservative planning screen. NASA-STD-3001 uses age/sex-specific REID, not this single number.

settlement_design_target_mSv_per_year.note: Analogy to ICRP occupational management, applied as a settlement design target. Not a NASA flight limit.

acute_injury_mSv.note: Deterministic effects become a medical concern around ~1 Gy acute whole-body. Dose equivalent is not the same quantity; this threshold is a game medical screen.

game_spe_probability_mars_mission.note: DRAMATIC COMPRESSION for play. MSL's cruise SEPs were a few percent of total dose during one solar-max transit. This is not a forecast of SPE frequency.

night_days_nonpolar.note: Half a synodic month. Polar sites are not in this night. Peaks of long illumination are not truly eternal; the game uses an estimate.

polar_illumination_fraction.note: Some south-pole ridge sites have high but not 100% illumination. 0.8 is a planning estimate, not an LRO product for a named peak.

water_ice_wt_fraction_cabeus.note: One crater's ejecta, not a global average and not a proven minable reserve.

surface_pressure_mb.note: Mean. Varies roughly from ~4 to ~9 mb with season and weather.

distance_min_m.note: DRA comparison table order: ~58e6 km at the near end; 5.46e10 m used so that one-way light time is ~3 minutes.

distance_max_m.note: DRA far end ~400e6 km. One-way light time ~22 minutes; two-way ~44 minutes.

synodic_days.note: Earth-Mars synodic period. Opportunities about every 26 months. The 15-year cycle modulates energy; this game slips to the next opportunity but does not model every porkchop.

window_half_width_days.note: A practical departure month, not a Lambert-solution window.

window_reference_date.note: Anchor near the late-2026 Mars departure season. Later windows are this date plus integer synodic periods.

perchlorate_wt_fraction_phoenix.note: Mid of the ~0.4–0.6 wt% Phoenix WCL result. Not a global mean. Curiosity and later work show perchlorate and oxychlorine compounds are widespread enough that untreated regolith is a bad growth medium.

dust_storm_solar_fraction.note: Global storms can cut surface sunlight to a small fraction of clear-sky. 0.15 is a planning estimate, not a named storm's optical depth.

heritage_landed_mass_t.note: Order of one tonne. Curiosity/Perseverance-class. Not a human lander.

isru_pilot_o2_kg_per_year.note: Game gate for a pilot plant: ~0.11 kg/h if run all year, about 10× MOXIE's peak and continuous. Still not a full ascent load.

ascent_o2_store_kg.note: Order-of-magnitude oxidizer load for a SMALL ascent of people off Mars. DRA-class vehicles can be larger. Not a propulsion design.

surface_to_leo_with_losses.note: Planning value: ~7.8 km/s orbital plus gravity and drag losses. Actual losses depend on the vehicle.

leo_to_tli.note: LEO to trans-lunar injection, Apollo-class planning value ~3.1–3.2 km/s.

llo_to_surface.note: No lunar atmosphere. The propellant is not optional.

leo_to_tmi_min_energy.note: Minimum-energy trans-Mars injection from low Earth orbit, planning value. Fast crew trajectories cost more. DRA's published maneuver table is for specific assembly orbits and NTR vehicles and is not this number.

mars_terminal_descent.note: Propulsive terminal descent after aerocapture/entry. Highly architecture-dependent.

mars_edl_systems_overhead.note: Extra factor so a naive rocket equation does not pretend a rover's landed mass is the whole entry system.

hydrolox_vacuum_isp_s.note: Round vacuum hydrolox planning value. RL10-class engines are in this neighborhood and some variants are higher (~465 s).

storable_isp_s.note: Storable bipropellant vacuum planning value for lunar descent/ascent.

ntr_isp_s.note: Midpoint of the DRA 5.0 ~900–910 s NERVA-derived figure. Not a flight-proven stage.

ntr_imleo_multiplier.note: Game factor so an NTR campaign sits in the DRA 800–1200 t band while the chemical campaign sits above it. The rocket equation itself is exact; this campaign multiplier is the estimate.

mars_preposition_imleo_t.note: Fixed cargo-preposition share of IMLEO for a 6-person-class campaign. Estimate anchored to DRA's hundreds-of-tonnes campaign, not a vehicle CAD model.

lunar_sortie_imleo_t.note: Two-crew short lunar sortie, full stack in LEO, including return. Estimate.

reference_outbound_days.note: Inside the DRA ~180–210 day transit band. One worked example in the literature is 174 days out and 201 back.

reference_surface_days.note: Inside the DRA long-stay band (~500–540 days). A worked example is 539 days.

reference_vehicles.note: Education only. The game buys vehicle classes, not a branded manifest.

biosphere2_o2_low_percent.note: Commonly cited low near 14.2–14.5%. The paper is the source of the decline; the single endpoint is quoted as an estimate of the reported low.

independence_years.note: Design rule of this game, chosen so a stockpile cannot fake a civilization. Five years of local surplus.

food_local_fraction.note: Design rule: ≥90% of dry edible calories grown on site.

industrial_closure.note: Fraction of critical spare-part mass fabricable locally. Design rule.

population_with_archive.note: NOT a genetically viable population by itself. Requires the archive and births below.

genome_archive_donors.note: Game-scale germplasm/genome archive. Smith's no-bank census is far larger; the archive is what makes a small settlement a seed rather than a genetic bottleneck pretending to be a species backup.

population_without_archive.note: Lower order of Smith's published census range. Still an estimate relative to his scenario assumptions (world ship, not Mars).

foothold_days.note: Conjunction-class Mars surface stay. DRA 5.0's long-stay band is about 500–540 days; one worked example is 539. The game uses 500. Mars-500's 520 days were an Earth isolation study, not a surface stay.

foothold_month_days.note: The settlement ledger advances in 30-day months. Seventeen of them are 510 days, which clears 500.

foothold_min_population.note: One person is a castaway. Two is the smallest crew that can keep a watch. Not a genetic population.

foothold_food_local_fraction.note: A quarter of dry edible mass grown on site. Enough that the crew is not living on a shipped pantry. The ember still requires 0.90. Estimate.

foothold_o2_local_fraction.note: At least half of metabolic oxygen from ISRU plus plants. Current Sabatier recovery is about 47%; a foothold has to clear that order with local oxygen, not bottled gas alone. The 0.50 threshold is an estimate set just above that demonstrated recovery.

foothold_water_local_fraction.note: Local ISRU water covers at least half of unrecovered wastewater. The rest may still ride in tanks. The ember requires every litre of makeup to be local.

foothold_power_margin.note: Worst-case power (lunar night or a dust storm) must meet demand. The ember asks for 1.2. A foothold asks not to go dark.

foothold_dose_mSv_per_year.note: ICRP 103 manages planned occupational exposure at 20 mSv/year averaged over 5 years, and not more than 50 mSv in a single year. A 500-day foothold is closer to one hard year than to a permanent settlement, so the game uses 50. The ember stays at 20. Analogy, not a NASA flight limit.

foothold_human_years.note: A multi-generational human tier, about four generations if a generation is taken near 25 years. The 25 is a round figure, not a measured settlement lifetime. This is not Smith's census and not a new species.

foothold_century_min_population.note: Same household floor the birth rule already uses. Two people keeping a watch are not a next generation.

foothold_century_min_births.note: At least one off-world birth. Aging in place is not a second generation.

foothold_biology_years.note: Established tier. Biosphere 2 lost control of oxygen over roughly two years. Ten years is a design rule: several times longer than that closed-system failure, long enough to call a sheltered niche established, and still not speciation. Estimate.

foothold_biology_deep_years.note: Speciation-scale tier for a sheltered Earth lineage. Hendry, Nosil, and Rieseberg (2007) show ecological speciation has no single clock: some cases are a few hundred generations, many animals are closer to a million years. The owner's ask is thousands to tens of thousands of years. The game uses 10,000 years and marks it as an estimate. It is not a claim that a moss becomes a new species on a schedule. It is also not the Lenski long-term evolution experiment: that experiment's 10,000 generations are years of flasks, not 10,000 calendar years. See ltee_generations.

ltee_generations.note: Cited so it is not confused with the 10,000-year tier. Lenski and Travisano (1994) reported adaptation and divergence after 10,000 generations of E. coli. At roughly six to seven generations a day, that is a few years of continuous culture, not ten thousand years.

foothold_machine_years.note: Autonomous replicator tier. The 1980 NASA/ASEE summer study, published as NASA CP-2255 (1982), is a concept for a lunar factory that could maintain and grow itself. It was not built. Fifty years is this game's estimate of long enough to mine, reject heat, replace dead units, and copy with drift — not a duration from that study, and not a construction procedure.

foothold_machine_deep_years.note: Machine-tended life reaches the same 10,000-year speciation-scale estimate as the biological deep tier. The machines are the gardeners. The evolving thing is the living culture. Estimate, with the same caveat as foothold_biology_deep_years.

foothold_biology_min_level.note: Two successful culture runs on that world. One exposure is a sample. A tardigrade exposure never counts.

foothold_bio_water_kg_year.note: A trickle of locally produced water for a sealed niche, not a crew's wastewater. Open Martian air does not supply stable liquid water.

foothold_bio_power_kwe.note: Heat and a little light for a small dome. Not a human farm. Worst-case power: lunar night or a dust storm.

foothold_bio_shield_g_cm2.note: A berm or buried roof so the niche is not open sky. This is about UV and desiccation, not the human dose target. A greenhouse counts without this number. Open regolith does not.

foothold_culture_accessions.note: Strains and seeds banked per successful off-world culture. Not a count of cells, and not Smith's human census.

foothold_machine_robots.note: A maintainer set that can lose a unit and still have a spare. One rover is a visitor.

foothold_machine_industry.note: Alternate repair gate: half of critical spare mass made locally. The explicit repair fraction is the other gate. The ember still requires 0.8.

foothold_machine_power_kwe.note: Kilopower-class electric power so a robot crew survives lunar night or a dust storm. The 5 kWe figure is a round estimate inside the 1–10 kWe class, not a claim that one KRUSTY unit has been flown. Machines do not need oxygen.

foothold_machine_heat_floor_kwe.note: Minimum radiator capacity when there is no fission plant. Electronics, motors, and any habitat still dump heat, and vacuum has no air to carry it. Estimate.

foothold_machine_heat_per_kwe.note: Thermal kilowatts the radiators must reject per electric kilowatt of fission. Fission plants reject more heat than they deliver as electricity. Four is a round estimate in the Kilopower class, not a measured radiator curve for a named reactor.

foothold_machine_metal_t_year.note: A trickle of structural metal from local ore, enough that replacement parts are not shipped from Earth. The NASA study discusses processing lunar material. This one-tonne-per-year floor is an estimate, not a figure from that study.

foothold_machine_ore_t.note: Minimum surveyed ore still in reach. A body smaller than this is a sample, not a mine. The seed factory delivers a much larger local deposit. Estimate.

foothold_machine_repair_fraction.note: Fraction of the machine population replaced per year. Must meet or beat the failure fraction. Estimate. Not a maintenance manual.

foothold_machine_failure_fraction.note: Baseline fraction of units that die per year if nothing replaces them. The repair rate has to clear this. Estimate.

foothold_machine_fidelity_min.note: Copy fidelity. von Neumann's self-reproducing automaton is a theoretical existence argument, not a measured error rate and not a probe. 0.90 is this game's estimate of 'copies still resemble the original after decades.' Below it, the next epoch is refused.

foothold_machine_archive_accessions.note: A local microbe and seed bank so machines can re-establish a living culture. Required for the machine-tended deep tier, not for the 50-year replicator tier. Far smaller than the ember's 10,000-donor human archive. Not a release procedure.

replicator_metal_t_year.note: Metal rate a landed replicator seed is assumed to reach. Estimate, above the one-tonne floor. The game does not describe the refinery.

replicator_ore_reserve_t.note: Surveyed local ore delivered with the seed factory. At 2 t/year this is 50,000 years of feedstock, enough for the deep tier and not a model of a planetary crust. Estimate.

replicator_heat_reject_kwe.note: Radiators shipped with the seed, sized for about 10 kWe of fission at the 4 kWt per kWe estimate. A later 500 kWe reactor has to bring its own radiators.

replicator_repair_fraction.note: Replacement rate of a fresh seed factory. Above the 0.08 failure fraction. Estimate.

replicator_fidelity.note: Starting copy fidelity of a fresh seed. Above the 0.90 floor, with room for drift. Estimate. Not a measured mutation rate of a machine.

epoch_decade_years.note: One epoch step. Ten calendar years. Design rule.

epoch_century_years.note: One epoch step. One hundred calendar years. Design rule.

epoch_millennium_years.note: One epoch step. One thousand calendar years. One action, one risk roll. Ten of these reach the 10,000-year tier. Design rule.

epoch_demo_months.note: Closed or autonomous demonstration before the first epoch on that path. Biosphere 2 lost oxygen control on a roughly two-year run. The game asks for twelve engine-months, one year, before it will fast-forward. Estimate, and shorter than that historical failure.

epoch_stable_roll.note: d100 at or above this: the epoch fully elapses. Estimate.

epoch_strained_roll.note: d100 at or above this, and below stable: half the years elapse. Estimate.

epoch_setback_roll.note: d100 at or above this, and below strained: that path's epoch-years are halved and none are added. Below this, the epoch-years collapse to zero. Estimate.

epoch_earth_end_decade.note: A separate d100 at or below this ends Earth's program during a 10-year epoch. About a twentieth. Estimate, not a historical frequency.

epoch_earth_end_century.note: d100 at or below this ends Earth's program during a 100-year epoch. Estimate.

epoch_earth_end_millennium.note: d100 at or below this ends Earth's program during a 1,000-year epoch. A millennium is longer than an institution. More likely than not is an estimate, not a claim about any real century.

epoch_fidelity_strain.note: Replication-fidelity loss on a strained machine epoch. Halved if the line has already improved itself. Estimate of drift, not a bit-error rate.

epoch_fidelity_setback.note: Fidelity loss on a setback. Estimate.

epoch_fidelity_collapse.note: Fidelity loss when a machine epoch collapses. Estimate.

epoch_improvement_roll.note: A stable machine epoch at or above this roll sets replication_improvement: copies that are better than the parent. The NASA study hoped a factory could grow in capability. This flag is that hope as a die roll. It is not required for the 50-year tier, and it is not a design.

foothold_pp_political_cost.note: Diplomatic cost of putting Earth life on another world even inside a sealed niche. Not a COSPAR calculation and not a sterilization procedure.
